how_to_run: Run every command from the project folder with bash, in this order: test, build, expected_build (set EXPECTED), variables, preflight, deploy (only after the owner's yes in the chat), live_check, live_page_check, pages_check, after. Run all commands of one release in the same shell so the variables stay set. '<name>' inside a command means the command string in the field of that name in this file, pasted in whole (each rule is written once). A command that exits non-zero stops the release. Never print a token. Dry run (no yes from the owner): run everything up to preflight, then deploy_dry_run, and stop.
release_tag_rule: The release tag is v$VERSION (page v4.5 gives tag v4.5). EXCEPTION (R7): if the tag v$VERSION ALREADY EXISTS and the master is UNCHANGED since that tag, the release tag is v$VERSION-r2 (then -r3 and so on). 'Unchanged' is judged by build id: the build id in that tag's version.json (docs/version.json, or version.json at the root for v4.4 and v4.5, which predate the master being in git) equals the freshly built id in $EXPECTED. If the tag exists but the ids differ, STOP: the version was not bumped. release_tag is the only copy of this rule as a command; use its output as $TAG.
release_tag: if ! git rev-parse -q --verify "refs/tags/v$VERSION" >/dev/null; then echo "v$VERSION"; else OLD=$( (git show "v$VERSION:docs/version.json" 2>/dev/null || git show "v$VERSION:version.json") | python3 -c "import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)['build'])" ); if [ "$OLD" = "$EXPECTED" ]; then n=2; while git rev-parse -q --verify "refs/tags/v$VERSION-r$n" >/dev/null; do n=$((n+1)); done; echo "v$VERSION-r$n"; else echo "STOP: tag v$VERSION exists but its build id ($OLD) differs from the new build ($EXPECTED): bump the version" >&2; exit 1; fi; fi
previous_tag_use: Run it in the variables step, BEFORE the release commit and tag, and record the result as $PREV in the release record. Do not run it again at rollback time (it would return the new tag).
variables: NAMED='debt-snowball.html build_standalone.py tests docs README.md LICENSE .gitignore .nojekyll dev/release.json'
variables_use: Set them after expected_build ($TAG needs $EXPECTED and $VERSION). $NAMED is used unquoted on purpose (no path in it has a space); $ALLOWED is the one list of paths a release may stage.
preflight: git config --local --get-all credential.https://github.com.helper | grep -q 'gh auth token --user ElectricBuffaloApps'
expected_build_use: EXPECTED=$(<expected_build>) straight after the build. If the master is unchanged since $PREV, EXPECTED must equal the id in the previous release record.
deploy: bad=$(git diff --cached --name-only | grep -E ' [0-9]+(\.[^/ ]*)?$'); if [ -n "$bad" ]; then echo "STOP: iCloud conflict copies are staged: $bad. Unstage them (git restore --staged -- <path>), delete the copies, start again"; false; fi
bad=$(git diff --cached --name-only | grep -v -E "$ALLOWED"); if [ -n "$bad" ]; then echo "STOP: staged paths outside the named list: $bad"; false; fi
deploy_notes: Named paths only, never git add -A or commit -a, never --force. The two guards after the add stop the release on an iCloud conflict copy ('name 2.ext') or any path outside $ALLOWED. The commit runs only if something is staged (a re-release of an unchanged master may stage nothing; the tag then goes on the current commit).
pages_check_use: GET only. After any push to main: source.path must be /docs and builds/latest must have status built for the pushed commit (pages_wait proves it).
pages_wait: start=$(date +%s); ok=; while :; do P=$(GH_TOKEN=$(/opt/homebrew/bin/gh auth token --user ElectricBuffaloApps) /opt/homebrew/bin/gh api repos/ElectricBuffaloApps/debt-snowball/pages 2>/dev/null); B=$(GH_TOKEN=$(/opt/homebrew/bin/gh auth token --user ElectricBuffaloApps) /opt/homebrew/bin/gh api repos/ElectricBuffaloApps/debt-snowball/pages/builds/latest 2>/dev/null); if P="$P" B="$B" WANT_PATH="$WANT_PATH" WANT_COMMIT="$WANT_COMMIT" AFTER="$AFTER" python3 -c 'import os,json; p=json.loads(os.environ["P"] or "{}"); b=json.loads(os.environ["B"] or "{}"); path=(p.get("source") or {}).get("path"); st=b.get("status"); c=b.get("commit") or ""; at=b.get("created_at") or ""; print("pages: source.path %s, latest build %s, commit %s, created %s (want %s, %s, after %s)" % (path, st, c[:7], at, os.environ["WANT_PATH"], os.environ["WANT_COMMIT"][:7], os.environ["AFTER"] or "-")); raise SystemExit(0 if path == os.environ["WANT_PATH"] and st == "built" and c == os.environ["WANT_COMMIT"] and at > os.environ["AFTER"] else 1)'; then ok=1; break; fi; [ $(( $(date +%s) - start )) -ge 600 ] && break; sleep 20; done; if [ -n "$ok" ]; then echo "PAGES OK"; else echo "PAGES NOT PROVEN after 600 s (last state above)"; false; fi
pages_wait_use: GET only. Set these shell variables first: WANT_PATH (/ or /docs), WANT_COMMIT (full hash: git rev-parse) and AFTER (a created_at read with latest_build_at BEFORE the push or PUT being proved). Passes only when Pages serves WANT_PATH and builds/latest is status built, for WANT_COMMIT, created later than AFTER. AFTER is GitHub's own clock, so the Mac's clock cannot fool it; a build from before the push or PUT can never pass. Polls every 20 s and stops on 600 s elapsed.

live_check.command: start=$(date +%s); got=; while :; do got=$(curl -fsS -m 15 "https://electricbuffaloapps.github.io/debt-snowball/version.json?cb=$(date +%s)" | python3 -c "import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)['build'])" 2>/dev/null); [ "$got" = "$EXPECTED" ] && break; [ $(( $(date +%s) - start )) -ge 600 ] && break; sleep 20; done; if [ "$got" = "$EXPECTED" ]; then echo "LIVE OK $got"; else echo "NOT LIVE after 600 s: last saw '$got', wanted $EXPECTED"; false; fi

live_page_check: if curl -fsS -m 15 "https://electricbuffaloapps.github.io/debt-snowball/?cb=$(date +%s)" | cmp -s - docs/index.html; then echo "PAGE OK"; else echo "STOP: the live page did not load or differs from docs/index.html"; false; fi

rollback.works_for: v4.5-r2 and every later tag. v4.4 and v4.5 hold the site at the repo root, not in docs/; the first step refuses them. For those, redeploy by hand with the owner.
steps: if git cat-file -e "$PREV:docs/index.html" 2>/dev/null && git cat-file -e "$PREV:docs/version.json" 2>/dev/null; then echo "$PREV has docs/"; else echo "STOP: $PREV has no docs/ site (it predates the docs/ layout). Do not roll back this way; tell the owner"; false; fi
rollback.then: EXPECTED=$(git show "$PREV:docs/version.json" | python3 -c "import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)['build'])"), then live_check and pages_check. Say in the report that a rollback happened and why.

after.artifact_republish: Only if the master changed since the last release tag, i.e. $TAG has no -rN suffix (an -rN tag means the build id was unchanged). If changed, tell the owner to republish the claude.ai artifact from debt-snowball.html in the browser (its URL is in dev/private-notes.md, which is not tracked). If unchanged, say 'artifact unchanged'.
after.portfolio: (cd ../.. && python3 Dev/portfolio.py set debt-snowball live_version=$VERSION last_release=$(date +%F))
after.portfolio_use: The subshell runs it from two levels up and leaves the shell in the project folder.
after.release_record: dev/release-<yyyy-mm-dd>.md: version, build id, commit, $TAG, $PREV, what changed, test counts, live check result, pages_check result, rollback command. Then `git add -- dev/release-<yyyy-mm-dd>.md`, commit, and push with the same yes. That push starts a Pages build: prove it with pages_wait (WANT_COMMIT = the record commit), then live_check and live_page_check.

runner_notes: Found by the release dry run of 12/11/2026.
Run under bash, not zsh: zsh does not split $NAMED into words (git add fails with exit 128). From a zsh tool shell, wrap each step in bash -c or put the steps in one bash script.
export every variable (EXPECTED, VERSION, PREV, TAG, NAMED) so later steps and child shells see it; an unexported EXPECTED makes live_check wait the full 600 s.
The waits can take up to 600 s each: give the tool call a timeout of at least 660 s or run the wait in the background.
Do not run under set -e: the guards print STOP and return false on purpose.

When the master is unchanged nothing is staged, no commit is made and the tag goes on the current HEAD; live_check then proves only that the site is still up, and pages_wait is the proof of the release.
The release record is pushed after the release: run pages_wait and live_check once more after that push.
